sourceInformation.genre: Train driving simulation with arcade scoring
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person cab view (pseudo-3D), with chase and platform cameras, and a Halo Map for stage select
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 (full engine, handoff package) with a custom rail renderer; AI Hub session client 1.4.0; vanilla JavaScript; Node and Playwright 1.63.0 for tests
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's PS1-era pixel style; new code-drawn trains, cab, signals, stations and townscape
sourceInformation.animation: Code-tweened gloved call, crossing gates, speed needle, notch cells, judgment banners and the Stop Cam; Humanoid rigs in briefing portraits only
sourceInformation.audio: All procedural: Web Audio traction, rolling, wind and brake layers; chip sound effects; 12 departure melodies; gibberish voices by syllable synthesis
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub session, ghost mode, 2 to 4 players (Session Protocol 1); local two-player duel on one keyboard
sourceInformation.testing: One headless command (node test/run.mjs, 135 checks), Playwright browser checks, a mock hub contract, a scripted playthrough of every stage, and the real AI Hub harness (2 players, 4 players with latency and loss, host leaves)
sourceInformation.research: Read the engine handoff docs and the AI Hub protocol; no web research
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux (WSL2); Chromium via Playwright for the browser checks

testingFeedback: About twenty issues changed the code, from rail drawing and the autopilot to the timetable and the Halo Time start value.

About six were critical: the rail drew nothing; the autopilot got stuck in emergency braking; Halo Time started at zero; a permanent 25 km/h cap; strips were attached only to their first segment; parked trains left the blocks.
The most helpful were the stop-accuracy runs from several starting states, and the real AI Hub harness, which confirmed the hub contract.
The least helpful were the stub draw and the screenshot checks: they catch exceptions and layout, not how the game feels.
engineFeedback: The fixed step with game.advance, the scene system, the pixel primitives, E.Dialog and E.Menu.

The road module needed a fork rather than a drop-in; the settings-group filter was not used; scene data for game.start was unclear; the standard Quit row is removed by setting menu.quit to false at runtime, which the docs do not state.
The rail renderer, the train model, the signal and stop logic, the autopilot and the dev sliders: all built here.
Nothing in the engine was changed. Dev Mode, the duel, the Stop Cam and the hub screens are the game's own code.
Nothing in the engine was changed. Dev Mode and the settings are the game's own screens.
A font with common UI symbols, and a documented settings-group filter for dev screens.
promptFeedback: The plan with checkable numbers: the check values made the physics testable.
The scope (about fifty subsystems) against one session; the plan and TASK disagree on file layout in places; and the strict every-feature condition cannot be met by partial builds.
Getting an end-to-end game with tests in one session; several features had to be cut.
A priority order with a minimum to ship, a time budget per milestone, and a per-feature acceptance list that counts partial builds as open.

aiHub.name: Densha de Halo!
aiHub.tagline: Stop on the mark. Leave on the second.
aiHub.description: Drive the Halo Line, a loop railway around Akari City, from the first train at dawn to the last train at night: stop exactly on the mark, keep the timetable to the second, and point and call every signal. Race up to three friends on the four-track Parallel Run.
aiHub.controls: Lever W/S or L2/R2 · Call E/✕ · Horn Space/□ · ATS Q/△ · EB Backspace/L1
